title: Make a component out of what you drew, and find it in the Library
goal: Turn a group you drew into a reusable component: it takes a name, wears a badge on the canvas so you can tell it apart, and shows up in a Library panel you can browse. Placing copies of it comes next.
notes:
Flag: next-components, Next only. Follow docs/design/ui-building.md, which this task depends on, for where components are stored and what the Library panel is. The mock is docs/design/mocks/pages/component-configure-wt.html steps one and two, and components.html for the Library panel with its scopes. Placing an instance, overrides and variants are later tasks. This slice stops at making one and seeing it listed. Depends on the layers list showing groups, and on the spec page.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). The payoff rung: make one, then find it in the Library.
acceptance: The Layer menu gains Make Component with Option Command K, enabled when a group is selected
The new component is listed in a Library panel with its name and a small picture of itself, and renaming it in one place renames it in both
The main component is marked on the canvas and in the layers list so it is never mistaken for an ordinary group

Try it: open Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, flags next-layer-groups and next-components on, draw a box and a label, group them, press Option Command K, name it Setting, and find Setting in the Library
Audit written under queue/audits/, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review BEFORE building. (1) The mock's Component section is mostly later work: property rows, 'Instances: main only', control/variant pickers, 'Add property'. All cut for this slice, which stops at make one and find it. (2) The mock never says how the thing gets named. A modal name dialog is ceremony; the app already renames a layer inline in the layers list, so Make Component promotes and drops straight into that inline rename with the text selected. Type Setting, press Return. (3) The Library is off by default (View > Show Library), so a first-time user could press Make Component and see nothing happen anywhere they are looking. Make Component therefore reveals the Library and switches it to Components, because the whole point of the command is that the thing lands on a shelf. Departure from the mock, which assumes the shelf is already open. (4) A component's name IS its layer's name, one string, so 'renaming in one place renames in both' falls out rather than needing a sync. (5) Duplicating a main must not produce two layers claiming to be the same component, so reidentify mints a fresh component id and a fresh name. (6) A frame that is promoted would carry two labels above its top left (frame name plus component badge); the component badge replaces the frame label for that layer, so there is always exactly one. (7) Ungroup on a main is left working: it is undoable and there are no instances yet to break. Recorded in rough.

Adversarial review AFTER building, on the probe with Screen Recording granted. The first build put the layers row into inline rename after the command; the capture showed a row that had silently become editable and looked identical to one that had not, so naming moved to the Component section's Name field, which visibly IS a field, and that section moved up beside Frame so it is not below the fold. The playtest menus dump reports every Layer row disabled, including rows that are plainly live, so menu enablement could not be read from it; canMakeComponent is covered by core tests and the command itself ran, which is what proves the row was live. Left rough and recorded in the audit: nothing places a copy yet; Ungroup on a main quietly ends the component; the shelf keeps its full height for one tile (filed as the-library-shelf-takes-only-the-room-its-tiles); a component at the very top of the canvas has its mark clipped, the same limit a frame's name has.

Layer > Make Component (Option Command K) promotes a group to a main: GroupContent gained a componentID, the command opens the Library on Components and hands you the Name field New-Folder style, and the violet four-diamond mark reads on the canvas, in the layers list and on the shelf tile. One name in one place, so all four agree. Core Components.swift with 23 tests, full suite green (1738). Verified on the probe with Screen Recording granted via Scripts/playtest/component-walk.json: promote, type Setting, all four surfaces read Setting; picking the tile opens the component's section with Select on Canvas. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-03-components.json with three real window captures. Follow-up filed: the-library-shelf-takes-only-the-room-its-tiles.
